scope: Channel-auth Sanctum, webhook signature verification (Stripe + SenangPay), idempotency UNIQUE
session_a_heals_acknowledged: GOAL-CMS S-R3-P0-G heal: token-name discriminator instead of tokenCan() to bypass Sanctum '*' wildcard (routes/channels.php:42)
Guest-Echo-Bypass closure: hasRole('Admin') or hasRole('Tenant Admin') replaces bare branch_id===0 sentinel (routes/channels.php:50-53)
summary: Channel-auth Sanctum hardening is COMPLETE post-S-R3-P0-G heal (verified routes/channels.php:36-58). The BRAIN flag 'Pusher channel-auth observably broken via Sanctum wildcard' is STALE - the fix is in code. Webhook signature verification is robust on both providers: Stripe uses StripeClient\Webhook::constructEvent with explicit SignatureVerificationException handling; SenangPay uses hash_hmac sha256 with hash_equals (timing-safe). Idempotency middleware enforces scoped key = (branch_id, user_id, sha256(key)) with payload-hash conflict detection. DB UNIQUE index on (provider, webhook_id) is the atomicity floor for webhook idempotency.

findings.title: Broadcast auth endpoint observably blocked by CORS in test-e2e SYNC flow-6

evidence.detail: consoleErrors[0]: 'Access to XMLHttpRequest at http://localhost:8000/api/broadcasting/auth from origin http://127.0.0.1:8000 has been blocked by CORS policy: The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header has a value http...'. The flow was marked severity=OK because polling fallback masked the failure, but the channel-auth round-trip silently fails when host = 127.0.0.1 and APP_URL = localhost (or vice versa). Pusher auth never succeeds -> client never subscribes to private channels -> only polling delivers updates.
evidence.impact: In any environment where the kiosk/POS/KDS browser hits a different host alias than APP_URL, real-time push is silently disabled. Polling fallback masks the failure (UX-wise) but the SLA `outbox_dispatch_latency_p95 < 2s` is replaced by polling cadence latency (3-10s).
evidence.session_a_heal_relation: Independent of S-R3-P0-G channel-auth role heal - this is a transport-layer CORS issue, not the authorization callback.

findings.recommendation: Audit config/cors.php to ensure 'allowed_origins' includes both the APP_URL host AND any alias (127.0.0.1/localhost pair). Add a sentinel test that asserts /api/broadcasting/auth returns a CORS-compatible Access-Control-Allow-Origin header for the configured kiosk host pattern.
findings.owner_question: What is the APP_URL value in production, and is the in-store kiosk browser configured to hit the exact same host (FQDN, IP, alias)? If they differ, channel-auth has silently failed since the SPA was deployed.

findings.title: Stripe webhook secret config key inconsistent: handleWebhook reads config('services.stripe.webhook_secret'), but no audit confirms it's set in production

evidence.detail: If `config('services.stripe.webhook_secret', '')` is empty, the handler returns 500 'misconfigured'. Stripe retries on 5xx -> the misconfigured webhook would re-fire forever and clog Stripe Dashboard webhook delivery view. No production-config sentinel test verifies the value is set.
evidence.impact: Deploy-time misconfig surfaces as Stripe Dashboard alerts, not as a production blocker. Owner could miss it during silent V1 hardening windows.

findings.recommendation: Add a sentinel test (tests/Feature/Production/StripeWebhookSecretConfiguredTest) that asserts config('services.stripe.webhook_secret') is non-empty in any environment with Stripe gateway active. Optionally fail health-check in /api/health/ready when stripe.activation_guard.activation_gate_cleared=true AND webhook_secret=''.

findings.title: SenangPay webhook calls WebhookEvent::firstOrCreate AFTER signature verification - correct - but the gateway-lookup happens BEFORE

evidence.detail: Flow: 1) parse fields (line 65-79), 2) PaymentGateway::with('gatewayOptions')->where('slug','senangpay') lookup (line 83), 3) extract secret (line 94-104), 4) compute HMAC + hash_equals (line 107-121), 5) firstOrCreate (line 125-137). Steps 2-3 hit the DB BEFORE signature verification - an attacker can DOS by spamming malformed webhook posts (each generates 1 SELECT on payment_gateways + 1 join on gateway_options, no idempotency replay).
evidence.impact: Low-grade DOS amplifier - one HTTP request -> 2 DB queries even on rejected signatures. Mitigated by IP-based throttle (Wave 3c TrustProxies '*'), but the webhook routes likely bypass per-IP rate limiting (provider IPs are static).

findings.recommendation: Move the gateway lookup AFTER the cheap field validation but BEFORE the hash check (acceptable - the secret is needed for HMAC). Cache the gateway secret via Cache::remember('senangpay.secret', 3600, fn() => ...) to avoid 2 DB queries on every webhook. Verify per-IP throttle is NOT bypassed for /senangpay-webhook/ and /stripe-webhook/ routes.
findings.owner_question: Are /stripe-webhook/ and /senangpay-webhook/ exempted from the per-IP throttle? Provider IPs are static -> exemption is safer than rate-limiting them, but the rate limit on signature-rejected requests should still apply.

findings.title: config/idempotency.php enabled = env('IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED', false) - default OFF

evidence.detail: Middleware short-circuits at line 41 'if (! config('idempotency.enabled', false)) return $next($request);'. Only the app-layer DB UNIQUE (branch_id, idempotency_key) on `orders` and the WebhookEvent UNIQUE protect against double-execute when middleware is off. Cannot verify production env from here.
evidence.impact: If IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED=false in production .env, double-submit on counter-collect-confirm / cash-drawer-open / refund-with-counter-entry executes twice on retry. The recent C-P0-H heal expanded `required_routes` to 10 more URIs (config:31-50) but the middleware itself is the gate.

findings.recommendation: Production env hardening: set IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED=true explicitly in .env.production.example. Add to deploy checklist + health-check warning when enabled=false in APP_ENV=production.
findings.owner_question: Is IDEMPOTENCY_MIDDLEWARE_ENABLED currently set to true in production? Cannot verify from code; the config default is false.

findings.title: Idempotency middleware fail_open mode falls through to app-layer UNIQUE

evidence.detail: When IdempotencyStorageUnavailableException is thrown (Redis down), if config('idempotency.fail_open') is true the request bypasses middleware. Default is false -> returns 503. The fail_open mode relies on app-layer DB UNIQUE - which only exists for the routes that have explicit (branch_id, idempotency_key) UNIQUE indexes (orders table). The 10 new C-P0-H routes added to required_routes do NOT all have app-layer UNIQUE backstops (e.g. cash-drawer-open).
evidence.impact: If fail_open=true (potential prod setting for availability), Redis outage + concurrent retry of cash-drawer-open could open the drawer twice. orders are safe (UNIQUE backstop); cash-drawer / refund / change-status are NOT all safe.

findings.recommendation: Inventory which required_routes have app-layer UNIQUE backstops. For routes without one, document that fail_open MUST stay false. Add a unit test asserting fail_open=false in production environment.
findings.owner_question: What is the production setting of IDEMPOTENCY_FAIL_OPEN? Default is false (safe), but if production toggled it true for availability, the 10 C-P0-H routes need backstop audit.

findings.title: Broadcast::routes uses auth:sanctum middleware but no per-IP throttle on /api/broadcasting/auth

evidence.detail: Broadcast::routes(['prefix' => 'api', 'middleware' => ['auth:sanctum']]). No throttle middleware. A spammer with a valid token (e.g. revoked-but-not-yet-expired kiosk token) could hammer /api/broadcasting/auth to enumerate branch IDs (channel-auth returns true/false per branchId).
evidence.impact: Low. The auth callback returns boolean only; no payload exposed. Throttle would be defense-in-depth.

findings.recommendation: Add `throttle:60,1` to the broadcast auth middleware: Broadcast::routes(['prefix' => 'api', 'middleware' => ['auth:sanctum', 'throttle:60,1']]). 60 channel subscriptions per minute per token is generous and blocks enumeration.

keep_as_is: routes/channels.php token-name discriminator (lines 41-48) - blocks Sanctum '*' wildcard
